_note: Known US varieties and errors, keyed by denomination + year + mint mark. 'value_note' figures are rough ballparks for reference only - always check current auction results (Heritage, GreatCollections) and get anything significant authenticated by PCGS/NGC/ANACS before buying or selling.

varieties.name: 1909-S VDB Lincoln Cent
varieties.where: Reverse, bottom rim between the wheat stalks
varieties.look_for: The initials V.D.B. at the very bottom of the reverse rim, plus an S mint mark under the date on the obverse. Only 484,000 made.
varieties.magnification: 10x to confirm the S is genuine
varieties.beware: Heavily counterfeited - added S mint marks and altered dates are extremely common. Authentication is essential.
varieties.value_note: Four figures even in low grade.

varieties.name: 1922 'No D' Lincoln Cent (Die Pair 2)
varieties.where: Obverse, under the date where the D mint mark belongs
varieties.look_for: All 1922 cents were struck in Denver, so a 1922 with NO mint mark is abnormal. The valuable version (Die Pair 2) has a completely absent D AND a strong, sharp reverse. Weak-D examples from worn dies are common and worth far less.
varieties.beware: Many 1922 cents have had the D removed by tooling. Check for a flat spot or scratches where the D should be.
varieties.value_note: Strong-reverse Die Pair 2 is worth many hundreds to thousands; weak D is worth much less.

varieties.name: 1943 Copper (Bronze) Cent
varieties.look_for: 1943 cents should be silver-colored zinc-coated steel and MAGNETIC. A copper-colored 1943 cent that does NOT stick to a magnet and weighs ~3.11g (not 2.70g) is a candidate. Roughly 20 are known to exist.
varieties.magnification: n/a - use a magnet and a scale first
varieties.beware: The overwhelming majority are fakes: copper-plated steel cents (still magnetic) or altered 1948 dates (the 8 shaved into a 3). Magnet test first, then weight, then authentication.
varieties.value_note: Six figures. Do not clean it, do not sell it locally, send it to PCGS or NGC.

varieties.name: 1944 Steel Cent
varieties.look_for: 1944 cents should be copper-colored brass and NON-magnetic. A silver-colored 1944 cent that sticks to a magnet and weighs ~2.70g is a candidate.
varieties.beware: 1943 steel cents with altered dates are the usual fake.
varieties.value_note: Tens of thousands of dollars. Authenticate.

varieties.name: 1955 Doubled Die Obverse
varieties.where: Obverse - the date, LIBERTY, and IN GOD WE TRUST
varieties.look_for: Dramatic, obvious doubling of the entire date and all obverse lettering. Strong enough to see without magnification. The doubling is clearly separated, not a shelf.
varieties.beware: Machine doubling (flat, shelf-like, same height) is NOT this variety. Real doubled die shows two distinct rounded impressions of equal boldness. Also beware the 1955 'Poor Man's Doubled Die', which is just die deterioration and is worth about a dollar.
varieties.value_note: Well into four figures even in circulated grades.

varieties.name: 1969-S Doubled Die Obverse
varieties.where: Obverse - date, LIBERTY, IN GOD WE TRUST
varieties.look_for: Strong separated doubling on the date and lettering. The MINT MARK is NOT doubled (it was punched separately) - this is the key diagnostic.
varieties.beware: If the S mint mark is also doubled, it is machine doubling, not the real variety.
varieties.value_note: Five figures. Very rare.

varieties.name: 1970-S Small Date ('Level 7')
varieties.look_for: On the Small Date, the top of the 7 is level with the top of the 0 and 9, and LIBERTY is weak, especially the LI. On the Large Date the 7 sits noticeably lower.
varieties.value_note: Modest premium in circulated grades, more in uncirculated.

varieties.name: 1972 Doubled Die Obverse
varieties.where: Obverse - date, LIBERTY, IN GOD WE TRUST
varieties.look_for: Clear separated doubling, strongest on LIBERTY and the date. There are several 1972 doubled dies; DDO-001 is the strong, valuable one.
varieties.beware: The weaker 1972 doubled dies (002 through 009) are worth far less than DDO-001.
varieties.value_note: Hundreds for DDO-001.

varieties.name: 1982 Transition Year - 7 Varieties
varieties.look_for: 1982 exists as Large Date and Small Date, in both bronze (3.11g) and zinc (2.50g), at both P and D. WEIGH IT - that is the only reliable way to tell bronze from zinc. On the Large Date the 2 has a flat-topped base; on the Small Date the digits are smaller and rounder with the 2 having a curved base.
varieties.beware: The 1982-D Small Date BRONZE is the famous rarity here - only a handful confirmed. If you find a 1982-D Small Date weighing 3.11g, authenticate it.
varieties.value_note: Most 1982 varieties are common. The 1982-D Small Date bronze is worth five to six figures.

varieties.name: 1983 Doubled Die Reverse
varieties.where: Reverse - UNITED STATES OF AMERICA and ONE CENT
varieties.look_for: Strong separated doubling across the reverse lettering, especially E PLURIBUS UNUM and UNITED STATES OF AMERICA.
varieties.value_note: Several hundred dollars.

varieties.name: 1984 Doubled Die Obverse ('Doubled Ear')
varieties.look_for: A clear second earlobe below the main one. Also doubling in the beard.
varieties.magnification: 10x-20x - this one really needs the microscope
varieties.value_note: A few hundred dollars.

varieties.name: 1992 Close AM Reverse
varieties.look_for: On business-strike 1992 cents the A and M of AMERICA should be clearly SEPARATED (Wide AM). If the A and M nearly touch at their bases (Close AM - a proof reverse), it is the rare variety. Also check the designer initials FG near the Memorial base: on Close AM they sit farther from the building.
varieties.value_note: Thousands of dollars. Very rare - only a couple dozen known.

varieties.name: 1998/1999/2000 Wide AM Reverse
varieties.look_for: The reverse of these years should have a CLOSE AM (A and M nearly touching). If the A and M are clearly SEPARATED with a gap (Wide AM - a proof reverse), it is the variety. 1999 Wide AM is the scarcest of the three.
varieties.magnification: 10x-20x. Compare side by side with a normal cent from the same year.
varieties.value_note: 1999 Wide AM: hundreds. 1998 and 2000: tens of dollars. The 2000 is common enough to find in circulation.

varieties.name: 1995 Doubled Die Obverse
varieties.where: Obverse - LIBERTY and IN GOD WE TRUST
varieties.look_for: Clear doubling on LIBERTY, particularly the LIB. Weaker on IN GOD WE TRUST.
varieties.value_note: Modest - tens of dollars in high grade. Common enough to still find in rolls.

varieties.name: 2009 Formative Years DDO ('Extra Finger/Thumb')
varieties.where: Reverse of the 'Formative Years' (rail splitter) design - Lincoln's hand on the axe
varieties.look_for: An extra finger or thumb visible on the hand gripping the log, and doubling in the fingers.
varieties.value_note: Tens to low hundreds depending on grade and strength.

varieties.name: BIE Die Break (any Lincoln cent)
varieties.where: Obverse - between the B and E of LIBERTY
varieties.look_for: A small raised vertical bar between the B and E, making LIBERTY read like 'LIBIE RTY'. Caused by a small die crack filling with metal.
varieties.value_note: A few dollars. Common but fun to collect - many collectors specialize in these.

varieties.name: 1939 Doubled Monticello / Doubled FIVE CENTS
varieties.look_for: Clear separated doubling on the words MONTICELLO and FIVE CENTS.
varieties.value_note: Low hundreds and up depending on grade.

varieties.name: 1949-D/S Over Mint Mark
varieties.look_for: Traces of an underlying S visible beneath and around the D. Look for the curves of the S poking out of the D's openings.
varieties.value_note: Low hundreds in higher grades.

varieties.name: 1954-S/D Over Mint Mark
varieties.look_for: Remnants of a D underneath the S - look for the D's straight left stem and its corners inside the S.
varieties.value_note: Tens to low hundreds.

varieties.name: 1955-D/S Over Mint Mark
varieties.look_for: Traces of an S under the D.
varieties.value_note: Tens to low hundreds.

varieties.name: 2005-D 'Speared Bison'
varieties.look_for: A raised line running diagonally through the bison's body like a spear, caused by a gouge in the die.
varieties.value_note: Tens to low hundreds depending on grade.

varieties.name: War Nickel (35% silver)
varieties.where: Reverse - large mint mark ABOVE Monticello's dome
varieties.look_for: A large P, D, or S above the dome. This is the only US coin series where a P mint mark appears before 1979. 1942 exists both ways - only the ones with the large mint mark above the dome are silver.
varieties.value_note: Worth its silver melt value, typically a couple of dollars. Worth pulling out of any nickel roll.

varieties.name: 1982 No-P Roosevelt Dime
varieties.look_for: 1982 dimes from Philadelphia should have a P. A 1982 dime with NO mint mark at all, and a clean smooth field where the P belongs, is the error. This one actually reached circulation - it is findable.
varieties.magnification: 10x - check that the area is smooth, not tooled or worn
varieties.beware: Someone may have removed the P. Look for scratches, a depression, or disturbed field texture.
varieties.value_note: Low hundreds; more for a strong strike in high grade.

varieties.name: No-S Proof Roosevelt Dime
varieties.look_for: A PROOF dime (mirror fields, sharp frosted devices, from a proof set) of 1968, 1970, 1975, or 1983 that is missing its S mint mark. The 1975 No-S is the rarest - only two are known.
varieties.beware: This only counts on proof coins. A business-strike Philadelphia dime from those years legitimately has no mint mark and is worth face value.
varieties.value_note: 1968/1970/1983 No-S: four to five figures. 1975 No-S: over half a million dollars.

varieties.name: 1964-D Doubled Die Reverse
varieties.where: Reverse - ONE DIME and E PLURIBUS UNUM
varieties.look_for: Separated doubling on the reverse lettering.
varieties.value_note: Tens to low hundreds.

varieties.name: 1932-D and 1932-S Washington Quarter
varieties.look_for: First year of the Washington quarter with very low mintages at Denver and San Francisco.
varieties.magnification: 10x to verify the mint mark is not added
varieties.beware: Added mint marks are common. Authenticate.
varieties.value_note: Low hundreds and up even in worn condition.

varieties.name: 1937 Doubled Die Obverse
varieties.look_for: Strong separated doubling on IN GOD WE TRUST.
varieties.value_note: Hundreds and up.

varieties.name: 1943 Doubled Die Obverse
varieties.where: Obverse - IN GOD WE TRUST and LIBERTY
varieties.look_for: Doubling on the obverse motto and LIBERTY. The 1943-S is the stronger and more valuable of the two.
varieties.value_note: Low hundreds.

varieties.name: 1950-D/S and 1950-S/D Over Mint Mark
varieties.look_for: A D punched over an S (1950-D/S) or an S punched over a D (1950-S/D). Look for the underlying letter's edges emerging from the primary mint mark.
varieties.value_note: Low hundreds and up.

varieties.name: 1999-P Delaware 'Spitting Horse'
varieties.look_for: A raised die crack running from the horse's mouth forward, resembling spit.
varieties.value_note: A few dollars to low tens. Common but popular.

varieties.name: 2004-D Wisconsin Extra Leaf (High and Low)
varieties.where: Reverse - the ear of corn, left side
varieties.look_for: An extra leaf on the left side of the corn ear. 'High Leaf' points upward toward the top of the corn; 'Low Leaf' points downward. A normal Wisconsin quarter has no leaf there at all.
varieties.value_note: Low hundreds each in uncirculated grades.

varieties.name: 2005 Minnesota Doubled Die Reverse ('Extra Tree')
varieties.where: Reverse - the tree line behind the main trees
varieties.look_for: Extra or doubled trees in the background treeline. There are dozens of recognized die varieties for this one, of varying strength.
varieties.value_note: Tens of dollars for stronger varieties.

varieties.name: 2005 Kansas 'IN GOD WE RUST'
varieties.look_for: The T in TRUST is missing or nearly gone because grease filled that part of the die, making it read 'IN GOD WE RUST'.
varieties.value_note: Low tens of dollars.

varieties.name: 1970-S Quarter Struck Over 1941 Canadian Quarter
varieties.where: Whole coin - look for Canadian design traces
varieties.look_for: Traces of Canadian design underneath, and a weight around 5.83g rather than 5.67g.
varieties.value_note: Tens of thousands. Extremely rare.

varieties.name: 1964 Accented Hair Kennedy Half (Proof)
varieties.where: Obverse - Kennedy's hair above the ear
varieties.look_for: Heavier, more pronounced hair lines above and left of the ear, and the bottom-left serif of the I in LIBERTY is missing or very weak. Proof coins only.
varieties.value_note: Tens to low hundreds.

varieties.name: 1974-D Doubled Die Obverse
varieties.look_for: Clear doubling on IN GOD WE TRUST.
varieties.value_note: Tens to low hundreds.

varieties.name: 1982 No FG Kennedy Half
varieties.where: Reverse - between the eagle's tail feathers and leg
varieties.look_for: The designer initials FG (Frank Gasparro) are missing, polished off the die.
varieties.value_note: Tens of dollars.

varieties.name: 1979-P Wide Rim / Near Date SBA
varieties.where: Obverse - the rim and the date
varieties.look_for: On the Wide Rim (Near Date) the date sits noticeably closer to the rim, with a thicker rim. On the common Narrow Rim there is a clear gap.
varieties.value_note: Tens of dollars circulated, low hundreds uncirculated.

varieties.name: 2000-P 'Cheerios' Sacagawea Dollar
varieties.look_for: Enhanced, highly detailed tail feathers with distinct central shafts on each feather, versus the plain feathers on normal coins. These were distributed in Cheerios cereal boxes in 2000.
varieties.value_note: Thousands of dollars.

varieties.name: 2000-P Sacagawea/Quarter Mule
varieties.where: Obverse - Washington quarter design on a golden dollar
varieties.look_for: A golden dollar with the WASHINGTON QUARTER obverse and the Sacagawea eagle reverse. About a dozen known.
varieties.value_note: Six figures.

varieties.name: Presidential Dollar Missing Edge Lettering ('Godless Dollar')
varieties.look_for: Presidential dollars (2007-2016) have incused lettering on the edge including IN GOD WE TRUST, the year, and the mint mark. A completely PLAIN edge with no lettering at all is the error. Most common on 2007 George Washington dollars.
varieties.beware: Partial or weak lettering is not the same as fully missing. Also check for DOUBLED edge lettering and INVERTED edge lettering, which are separate collectible errors.
varieties.value_note: Tens to low hundreds depending on the president and grade.
